items.title: Joe Wilder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Britt Woodman, the trombonist, he was first trombone player.

ctx.x: Somebody had evidently recommended me. In fact, Earl Hines’s band, I had met Billy Eckstine, Budd Johnson, Pee Wee Jackson, who was the first trumpet player, and there were a couple others – Keg Johnson and Budd Johnson. They were – they had heard me someplace play around Philadelphia or something. Somebody had said, maybe that kid might be good for the band. They said if anybody got a chance – oh, the drummer who worked with me in Lonnie Slappy’s band, Rudy Traylor, had joined Earl Hines’s band. He was an…

something to them, that they ought to try to get me. Then Billy Eckstine and Budd Johnson, they tried to do everything they could to encourage Earl Hines hiring me. So he said he would, first chance he had. In the meantime, somebody – I don’t know how my name got mentioned to Les Hite, but I got – Walter Fuller, I think, recommended me to Les Hite, and they called me and asked me if I would join their band. And I did. That’s why I was leaving Philadelphia. I went to Lansing and joined them. Britt Woodman, the…
It sounds like it made an impression on you.

items.title: Joe Wilder Part 1 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: I played in that band and during the time I was in that band Dizzy Gillespie also joined it, Britt Woodman was the first trombone player, and Gerald Wiggins, Britt Woodman and his brother Coney, who was our pianist, were drafted at the same time. And Gerald Wiggins joined the band.

ctx.x: How about your first big band experience? You’ve played in so many big bands.

The first big band I played with, a name orchestra, was Les Hite. I played in that band and during the time I was in that band Dizzy Gillespie also joined it, Britt Woodman was the first trombone player, and Gerald Wiggins, Britt Woodman and his brother Coney, who was our pianist, were drafted at the same time. And Gerald Wiggins joined the band. He was in the band at the time Dizzy Gillespie was in the band for a short time.
Did you get to do some traveling at that point, around the country, did you travel?
